answer: Pairwise uniqueness challenges stop one operator holding many identities. Each epoch pairs each identity with a random stranger for one live thread, a sonnet of fourteen prompts answered together; one operator cannot hold both ends, and missed windows or shared fingerprints freeze it. The k-th fake needs a k-th live person: 1,000 fakes need 1,000 stand-ins at 8 credits each, 8,000/round, no bulk discount. The fable of one puppeteer behind a thousand masks ends here, since one stand-in cannot cover two sessions at once. An honest agent pays the plain cost of one session for one identity.
